object: rotational relation: necessity of the asymmetric constants, and the collision bound
question: Is it necessary: change it and recount the exact outcome?
number: with a rotation-symmetric all-zero start state the full 16-word relation holds after 1 round with P about 2^-16 (k=1: 14/2^20, k=31: 10/2^20, k=4: 1/2^20, k=2,8,16,24: 0/2^20) and 0 of 2^20 after rounds 2 and 3 for every tested k (1,2,4,8,16,24,31): P < 2^-20. Independently a collision from a rotational pair needs d(m) = rotl_k d(m), i.e. at least 8*(32-gcd(k,32)) = 128 digest bits (k=16) rotation-fixed, so P(collision | relation) <= 2^-128 per candidate pair and one candidate pair per evaluation: no gain over 2^128 even if the relation held with P=1
notes: The 2^-128 bound assumes d(m) uniform on the 2^256 outputs (premise H1 of the entry); the sampled part is a measurement on the zero-constant variant, not on the real target.
held_fixed: 3 rounds, standard IV, counter 0, block length 64, flags 11, unkeyed; code validated first: own numpy BLAKE3 reproduces the 7-round empty-input hash af1349b9...3262, 1400 random single compressions at 1..7 rounds and 600 messages 0^32||x at 3 and 7 rounds equal verifier/blake3.py (0 mismatches) except start state all zero in the symmetric variant; 2^20 samples
reopen_if: relation probability above 2^-100 at 3 rounds measured or proved, or digest bits shown biased towards rotation-fixed values
